text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois has been the Capitals' finisher during a bad stretch. He's scored five goals in his last six games, a four-game goal streak among them, and added a power-play goal against Jeremy Swayman in Boston on Saturday, all while Washington lost seven of his last eight.

He's played 16 games and has 6 goals and 13 points, after only 29 games last season. The 5v5 picture is the best part of it: the Capitals take 57% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly five points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey noted he faced 98th-percentile competition in his small 2025-26 sample, so he's not being sheltered.

The goals will cool. He's shooting 20% against a likely range of 11 to 17%, and his own chances add up to 3.9 expected goals, not six. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, on only seven games, had him carrying the puck in on 71% of his entries. If he keeps tilting the ice like this, the points will hold up better than the shooting.
